findings.description: The effective-effort calculation returns None immediately when the primary resolved no effort. If fallback reaches a CLI entry with legacy extra.effort or extra.reasoning_effort, the headless adapter still resolves and sends that value, but MODELINV omits effort_effective and reports effort_source as none. This violates the new field's stated contract to record the answering hop's wire value.
findings.failure_mode: A successful fallback invocation produces an audit envelope that incorrectly reports no reasoning effort despite the CLI receiving an explicit effort flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the effective effort from the dispatched adapter or resolve the answering hop's legacy extra fallback before calculating effort_effective. Preserve primary-request provenance separately.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.cross_file_justification: resolve_effort (cheval.py:921-924) returns a fourth source value `extra`; the MODELINV parameter contract (modelinv.py:497-499) and the emit-site comment (cheval.py:2834) both enumerate only `caller | catalog | none`, and the payload schema model-invoke-complete.payload.schema.json is touched in this PR.
findings.description: resolve_effort has four rungs and returns `"extra"` whenever a CLI primary (kind=cli / auth_type=headless) carries `extra.effort` with no `--effort` and no `params.default_effort` — a reachable path for every stock headless entry that still has the legacy key. The documented contract for `effort_source` (SDD D-2.3, the modelinv.py parameter comment, the cheval.py emit comment, and the dry-run label mapping) says three values. If the new trajectory payload schema encodes that three-value enum, every MODELINV event on such a hop carries an out-of-enum value.
findings.failure_mode: Trajectory validation (schema bats / jsonschema in tests or downstream consumers) rejects model_invoke_complete events with `effort_source: extra`; the event is dropped or the suite goes red the first time a headless primary resolves effort from extra.effort.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one: add `extra` to the documented enum and to model-invoke-complete.payload.schema.json (and the modelinv/cheval comments), or collapse the extra rung into `catalog` for the envelope. Add a test that emits an envelope with source `extra` and validates it against the payload schema.

findings.description: `effort` is resolved once against the PRIMARY entry and then (a) sent as CompletionRequest.effort to every fallback hop and (b) reported as `effort_effective` for the hop that answered. Two mis-reports follow. Under-report: primary HTTP with no default, chain falls to a claude-headless hop whose `extra.effort` is set — the adapter's own `_resolve_effort` still emits `--effort <extra>` but `_effort` is None, so `effort` and `effort_effective` are omitted from the envelope. Over-apply: primary anthropic HTTP with `params.default_effort: xhigh` falls to a CLI hop — that hop now receives the primary's catalog default instead of its own catalog/extra value, and the envelope reports it as `catalog`.
findings.failure_mode: MODELINV telemetry attributes the wrong effort (or none) to the answering hop; a fallback CLI hop silently runs at the primary's reasoning level rather than its own configured default.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run resolve_effort per hop inside the chain walker (or at minimum recompute `effort_effective` from the final hop's resolved entry, falling back to that hop's extra.effort when `_effort` is None) and record the final hop's source.

findings.description: The docstring promises fail-closed on any read failure, but `_find_project_root()` is evaluated outside the try block. If it raises (no `.claude` marker on the cwd walk, permission error on a parent dir) the exception escapes `complete()`/`health_check()`/`validate_config()` as an unclassified error instead of a clean `AgyOptInRequiredError`/False. Separately, the function re-parses both YAML layers and deep-merges the full System catalog on every call; `complete()`, `health_check()` and `validate_config()` each call it, so a review that walks the chain several times re-reads the whole catalog per hop.
findings.failure_mode: An uncaught OSError/ValueError from the root walk crashes the hop raw (non-walkable, unclassified) on a host where cheval is invoked outside a project tree; otherwise repeated full-catalog parses add latency to every agy dispatch and health probe.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the root resolution inside the try, returning False on any exception. Cache the result per process (or per root) with a small lru_cache, and consider passing the already-loaded hounfour config from cheval instead of re-reading.

findings.description: `_effort_on_wire` lazily imports the private `_effort_for_model` from anthropic_adapter and is evaluated inline inside the `emit_model_invoke_complete(...)` call AFTER the model has answered (cheval.py:2838). Any failure there — an unmapped level such as `max` (in `_EFFORT_LEVELS` but possibly not in the adapter's per-family table), a rename of the private symbol, or an adapter import-time dependency missing on a thin host — raises out of the emit, after spend has occurred, and takes the audit record with it.
findings.failure_mode: A successful completion ends with a traceback at emit time; the MODELINV event is never written and cmd_invoke exits non-zero despite a good answer.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the body of `_effort_on_wire` in try/except returning the requested effort (or None) on any error, and compute it into a local before the emit call so a failure cannot abort the audit write. Add a test with `default_effort: max` through the anthropic mapping.

findings.description: The catalog rung validates `params.default_effort` verbatim while the extra rung normalises with `str(...).strip().lower()`. A YAML `default_effort: High` or `default_effort: null` (the natural way to say "no default") is logged as an invalid value and ignored, whereas the same text under `extra.effort` is accepted. The two rungs of the same chokepoint disagree on what a valid value is.
findings.failure_mode: An operator who sets a correctly-spelled but capitalised catalog default gets a WARN and the vendor default, with no error; `default_effort: null` produces a spurious 'None is not one of ...' warning on every process.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise the catalog value the same way (`str(v).strip().lower()`), and treat `None` as 'key absent' rather than 'invalid'.

findings.cross_file_justification: complete() (agy_headless_adapter.py:124-125) raises AgyOptInRequiredError, a ConfigError; the adapter's own error-classification comments treat ConfigError as the hard-abort (non-walkable) class in cheval's fallback chain.
findings.description: The refusal is a `ConfigError`, which the adapter family uses for hard-abort/non-walkable failures. The docstring says planners read `failure_class` as 'not planned, never a failed voice', which holds for the bash/TS planners that filter before dispatch — but inside cheval's own chain walker a `gemini-headless` hop that is NOT terminal (any cli-first / prefer-cli Google chain, or an operator alias whose primary is `gemini-headless:*` with a `gemini-api` fallback) will abort the chain at the gated hop instead of walking to the HTTP hop.
findings.failure_mode: `cheval invoke` on a Google chain whose first hop is agy fails INVALID_CONFIG with opt-in off even when a `gemini-api` key is present and the next hop would have answered.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the chain walker skip hops whose `health_check()` is False / whose error carries `failure_class: opt_in_required` (walkable, like ProviderUnavailableError), or document that the gated hop is only ever terminal and add a test asserting a cli-first chain still reaches the HTTP hop with opt-in off.

findings.description: For a measured entry the expected value is now `min(entry["effective_input_ceiling"], cw − dmt)` and is compared to `entry["effective_input_ceiling"]` — a tautology except for the I2 invariant on the next line. Combined with the sibling `probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling if _measured` and the permanent `pytest.skip` of `test_write_operator_set_changes_only_the_entry_and_replaces_the_shortcut`, the suite no longer checks anything about the calibrated Opus 5.5 value beyond I2, and the only schema/input_bound validation of the writer's output is skipped on head.
findings.failure_mode: A future hand-edit of the calibrated entry (wrong `probed_ceiling`, missing `method`/`transport`, calibration block not matching the v3 schema) passes the catalog floor suite.
findings.suggested_fix: For measured entries assert the calibration block against `$defs.ceilingCalibration` and that `effective_input_ceiling == min(ceiling_calibration.measured_input_tokens, cw − dmt)`; replace the skipped writer test's precondition with a SYNTH-catalog variant so the jsonschema + input_bound checks run unconditionally.
